title: MV Learn RPG Maker MV - The Game

posts.author: CleanWater
posts.body:
Do you want to become an indie RPG developer? And want to learn how to make games in a fun and interactive way? Then you are in the right place!
Learn RPG Maker MV
is a game made with it's source files available, so you can open it on your own
RPG Maker MV
editor and see first hand how the game examples were made, while also playing the game and learning from it through specially made interactive tutorials.
With fully commented events and database, this game teaches the basics of RPG Maker engine, covers more complex functions and also delve into deeper aspects of game development and game design fundamentals, yet with a simple and comprehensive language.
Features​
With this game you will learn:
Core concepts
* present in every version of any
RPG Maker
;
How to create engaging maps;
Classic RPG design with practical examples;
How to create consistent game progression;
Puzzles and mini-games with events-only;
Many hints&tips for using the engine;
And more!
* What you have learned on this game tutorial can also be applied to other
RPG Maker
engines.

First Announcement! - Learn RPG Maker MV by CleanWater
Hello everyone! Learn RPG Maker MV is a project that born spontaneously from an interaction with an old friend of mine. He had purchased RPG Maker MV and asked me some questions about it's basic usage...
alneto.itch.io
Hello everyone!
Learn RPG Maker MV
is a project that born spontaneously from an interaction with an old friend of mine. He had purchased
RPG Maker MV
and asked me some questions about it's basic usage. Then, I created a small demo to teach him about the engine.
This project does the same and go even further. After finishing it, the user who have followed all the tutorials and examples in-game will be able to create his own games with all the tools available within the
RPG Maker MV
engine.
This is a work in-progress, which means that this project is far from being complete, but it already presents some nice examples to help those newcomers striving to learn the engine. Of course, your feedback is much appreciated, it's your feedback that will help shape the future lessons. I may also review the content of already published lessons.
I decided to publish this project before finishing it because everyone who adventured themselves in game development knows how time consuming developing a game can be. I'm also doing the teacher's work of planning lessons and I'm also working completely alone on this project, which makes things even worse for my side. So, I needed to resort to some sort of funding while I'm on this.
The Itch.io's store page will work as a mix of
Crowdfunding with Early Access
, where you are invited to support the game both financially and with worthy feedback.
Check below the progress of the project with the initial lessons plans. Some of the contents may change with time. Every progress will be posted as an announcement together with the new downloadable source files.
The Basics - 39,20%​
These lessons below teaches the basics of RPG Maker editor.

Example Game - 0%​
I hope this project to be so useful for you as it was to my personal friend!
See you next time,
Alysson L. Neto

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
I'm not going to condemn you for your work to help people and get a bit of money, these are all fine things. I do think it's a bit of an odd choice to do it now for MV - the software has been out for 6 years and has dozens of tutorials available, as written guides, YouTube videos, and other people with sample games like this.
And those are all existing, complete products, not something that's barely started and asking for financial help to finish it. Even if your teaching style is really good, why is that worth paying for and waiting for instead of using one of the very many options readily and completely available?
It would make more sense to me for you to do this for RPG Maker MZ, which is still new enough that you could jump on the early bandwagon before all of the established RPG Maker YouTube channels have complete tutorial series.

posts.author: CleanWater
posts.body:
@ATT_Turan
to be honest, I prefer Linux over Windows. It's been two years I'm using only Ubuntu as my OS and I'm really in love with it. I had some bad experiences with Windows and the process of dual-booting is really extenuating for Linux users. Besides, I already have my workplace all set and I don't want to loose it just because of one single software.
MZ is surely a great addition to the maker series and I would love to put my hands on my own copy someday, but MV is equally powerful on my honest opinion and capable of many great things. 6 years don't make it really old anyway, maybe it's our technology that's "evolving" too fast. We have persons releasing games with 2k/3 and XP still today and these games also sell well and some even got good attention from the media.
All my knowledge about the maker series came from previous versions (2k, 2k3 and XP, I must confess I skipped VX and VX Ace) and if you can master the core concept of the maker series, you will have mastered 90% of everything from any RPG Maker. In less than one week I got the hang of MV and started working in a game together with the aforementioned old friend of mine and even started to explain him the basics of the engine. The fact of being an experienced user of other game engine (Game Maker) also helped me to "broaden" my vision about game development with this maker.
By the way,
ProtonDB
is a database for Linux users to share their experiences with
Steam Proton
, which allows Linux users to run Windows games and software on Linux systems (similar to what WINE also do). You probably never heard of it before, and that's alright, it's something that even some Linux users aren't aware of too.

It would not.
@CleanWater
What would interest me more is you finishing a game. And then pointing towards that game, saying
"Play this. And if you like it, and want to make something similar. Then this a course/lesson for you, where I teach you exactly how."
This for me,
is perfect clarity.
On what I'll be getting out of your lessons.
And if you end up not delivering (because after the lessons, perhaps I still can't make the sort of game you made.) Then I would know exactly what questions to ask you. And what more lessons I can push out from you.
Right now, your promise is vague. (If it was free, no one would care. Because with free stuff, we take what we can get. But when it's paid, people tend to hold you more accountable.)
Side note:
You can also keep the original first sentence. And make some additions like so:
"Do you want to become the next biggest indie RPG developer? These lessons won't get you there, but it's a first step. What you learn here will be the foundation of your game making journey, all the way to the top."
Just an example. (You can have someone dream big. And then pull them back down.)
The idea is, you manage expectation, and don't promise what you cannot deliver.
~ Creating game dev foundations, that would stick with a person. Simple to understand, simple to deliver.
~ Make a person the next biggest indie RPG Developer. Very vague, practically impossible to deliver.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Having seen a bit of this... "Tutorial", it looks like you need to book an english course before trying to teach anyone anything.
"And WHAT should I call you" Though, arguably even that would rarely ever be said. People say "What's your name?"
"known as"
"IN this game tutorial." "We'll cover the concept of events". up to means nothing since there's no list of any kind, so "up until" is meaningless.
If there was like a previous lesson and a list of lesson topics, you'd say "We're covering the concept of events to game progression in this episode" or something to that effect.
"IN RPG Maker"
"EleCtronic"
Good idea to teach a beginner that atmosphere is unnecessary.
Ah yes, the essence of a tutorial. NOT explain things in detail. Why the heck did I play this, if it's so intuitive, you don't need to bother?
"YouR" game world.
"IN your heart"
MV doesn't use scripts.
There are many more things that are actively detrimental to anyone trying to learn RPG maker, like the part where you tell the player about having used a script call, and then proceed to neither show or explain the script, but I don't want to overload the server with these screenshots.
So in summary:
Even as a free tutorial, this is worthless. Delivering the tutorial in game form offers nothing. The "instructions" are poorly written, innacurate and barely legible. Even watching a youtube video would be more efficient, since you could at least recreate what's on the screen while watching the video. This tutorial covers nothing you couldn't just learn from the already included, interactive tutorial that's in the engine. Whatever you made is unproductive.
